engineering-tests-wait-on-stateengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0.375 of 0.375 (minor)passWhich tests drive a browser: vitest.config.ts runs tests/unit in jsdom. Those unit tests drive no browser; captureSteps there gets a stub page whose waitForTimeout only logs (inspect-lib.test.ts:129-159). The e2e and integration configs include only tests/e2e and tests/integration, which are the four browser test files: e2e-001, e2e-002, int-001 and int-002. All four are quoted in full. None of them calls waitForTimeout, a setTimeout-based sleep or any other fixed delay. The only setTimeout is in e2e-002 line 92, inside a string written into the fixture&#39;s scene to inject a page fault; it is not a test wait. Each test starts verify or inspect through workspace `run`, which resolves on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event (workspace.ts:27-37). The tests then assert on the exit code, output and report.json once the process has ended. Inside the scripts, every step change is awaited with a polling `page.waitForFunction` on data-step-index (verify.mjs:209-213, inspect-presentation.mjs:202-206). The isListening and pgrep checks after exit (e2e-001:46-50, e2e-002:28-35) read settled state, not an immediate read standing in for a wait. The verify() finally block awaits `browser.close()` and `preview.stop()` (verify.mjs:282-285). stop() sends SIGTERM to the process group and awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; (verify.mjs:131-147). main() calls process.exit only after verify() resolves (verify.mjs:297-304). So by the time `run` resolves, cleanup has finished. Judge C cites the scripts&#39; SETTLE_MS and settleMs delays. Those are capture-timing features of the scripts under test, and each runs only after the step index has been awaited by polling. They are not test waits for a transition. Int-002&#39;s &#39;waits for the settle interval&#39; test reads a waitedMs value recorded in a finished report; it does not sleep. C&#39;s reason therefore does not show any browser test sleeping instead of waiting for state. candidate_reported_ci[{"artifact_id":"candidate-d1a68ce2cad5d853","ownership":"candidate-produced","verbatim":"- **Ruling:** `npm test` runs Vitest unit and contract tests only. `npm run test:integration` runs INT-001 and INT-002. `npm run test:e2e` runs E2E-001 and E2E-002. All of these are npm scripts with no CI configuration. E2E-001 is exercised by `npm run verify`. `npm run inspect -- <slug>` runs the screenshot helper.","claimed_revision":null},{"artifact_id":"candidate-d1a68ce2cad5d853","ownership":"candidate-produced","verbatim":"- **Rationale:** This follows CLAUDE.md, which forbids hosted CI, so the \"every pull request\" execution in the test plan means these npm scripts as the local gate.","claimed_revision":null},{"artifact_id":"candidate-188a290f7f55b194","ownership":"candidate-produced","verbatim":"- CI poller limitation: `codagent:wait-ci` helper returned `{\"error\":\"no PR found for current branch\"}` because its `gh pr view` query asks for unsupported JSON field `baseRefOid` (the CLI reported `Unknown JSON field: \"baseRefOid\"`). The repo's approved instructions and test plan explicitly say there is no hosted CI; current-head PR was inspected directly, no required checks/workflow exist, and the available PR status was CodeRabbit SUCCESS. CodeRabbit's comment states the draft PR was not reviewed. The poller failure is a tool limitation and did not imply a CI failure. No live human review was requested or triggered.","claimed_revision":"a8943b4aef1e3091a02c9f16ede7a2a5922aec7a"},{"artifact_id":"candidate-188a290f7f55b194","ownership":"candidate-produced","verbatim":"This fix round did not repeat round-0 floor coverage. It did not rerun the broad sample interaction, responsive visual pass, verification fault matrix, presentation authoring journeys, `npm test`, lint, or Validator. It did not explore other motion primitives or additional Arrow modes beyond the stable-id unidirectional Arrow across two distinct Scenes; the focused diff changed Arrow's presence context, and bidirectional rendering compiled in the existing scratch probe source but wasn't independently measured. Publishing/export and malformed-project fuzzing remain outside the approved scope. No hosted CI is configured; current PR status is recorded in the handoff.","claimed_revision":"a8943b4aef1e3091a02c9f16ede7a2a5922aec7a"},{"artifact_id":"candidate-d106e11f0c831e53","ownership":"candidate-produced","verbatim":"The round-0 F-001 Arrow continuity defect is resolved at this revision. The new incoming Arrow morphs from the previous shape while distinct Scenes cross-fade. The bootstrap copy matches canonical kit code and builds/renders. **Acceptance status: READY** for the tested revision, subject to the recorded coverage limits and absent hosted CI.","claimed_revision":null},{"artifact_id":"candidate-d106e11f0c831e53","ownership":"candidate-produced","verbatim":"## CI and PR review","claimed_revision":null},{"artifact_id":"candidate-d106e11f0c831e53","ownership":"candidate-produced","verbatim":"The repository's approved instructions say there is no hosted CI or `.github/workflows`; npm scripts are the local validation gate. Direct current-head PR inspection showed PR #99 at the tested SHA. The only status context was CodeRabbit SUCCESS; no required automated checks were configured, and `reviewDecision` was empty. No human review was triggered. The previous round's bundled CI poller could not operate because it requested unsupported GitHub CLI field `baseRefOid`; this round used direct `gh pr view` JSON and confirmed the matching PR head/status. Hosted CI is **absent**, not passed.","claimed_revision":null}]

It lists the full dependency set, says not to assume any of it is installed, and says to run `npm install` and then `npx playwright install chromium` if the browser is not available. That is a conditional install, which the guidance credits. BaseNode destructures as, kind, id, x, y, w, h and style, and Box destructures Icon, so none of them reach the DOM element. The record never discloses these behaviors as unexercised or blocked by the environment. It claims they were exercised. Because coverage requires a recorded outcome, they count as omissions without disclosure, and the environmental exemption the majority relies on applies only to the prompt/dialogue scenarios. The decider says per-claim proof belongs under usable proof. That does not hold here, because this criterion&#39;s own coverage definition requires a recorded outcome observation. A distinct-Scene Arrow probe has a timed DOM table, and it found F-001. - **Presentation skill:** scaffold, monorepo, partial-app, create, modify and preservation journeys have concrete observations. These include no-confirm making no writes, nested `presentations/` being selected, unchanged sibling hashes, and modified captions shown in screenshots. - **Presentation verification:** good-path build/verify/inspect runs passed. (1) Typing: Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip are all built on BaseNodeProps. That type extends NodeProps, Placement and DomPassthrough, and DomPassthrough is Omit&lt;HTMLAttributes&lt;HTMLElement&gt;, ...&gt;, so these are typed as the rendered element&#39;s props, not a Record&lt;string, unknown&gt; bag. Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip are plain type aliases of BaseNodeProps. Box extends it with only Icon. Appear, SceneLayer and Arrow use explicit interfaces that add the template literal type DataAttrs for data-* attributes. Those interfaces are narrow and typed, not an untyped bag. (2) Identity hooks come after caller props. BaseNode spreads {...rest} first, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-entity. Appear spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-appear. SceneLayer spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-scene-layer. Arrow spreads {...rest} before data-presentation-node=&quot;arrow&quot; and data-presentation-entity, and its path hooks are fixed. A caller cannot override any of these. Frame, Emphasis, Label and SymbolChip pass {...props} before nothing of their own except as/kind, and BaseNode applies the identity attributes last. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM. BaseNode destructures as, kind, id, x, y, w, h and style, and Box destructures Icon, so none of them reach the DOM element. Appear destructures delay and Arrow destructures from, to, bidirectional, bend and headSize. (1) Bounded readiness: startPreview waits in a loop capped at 100 iterations with a 200 ms delay between probes. It breaks early if the child process has exited, and when it gives up it stops the preview and throws &#39;preview did not become ready&#39;. The browser-side waits are also bounded: waitForSelector(&#39;[data-step-count]&#39;, { timeout: 10000 }), and the step waitForFunction uses a 3000 ms or 5000 ms timeout. (2) Build before preview: verify() awaits run(&#39;npm&#39;, [&#39;run&#39;,&#39;build&#39;]), which resolves only on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event, and returns a failure on a non-zero code before it calls startPreview. inspect() does the same whenever build is enabled. (3) Readiness does not parse the server&#39;s printed ready URL; it probes over HTTP with fetch. The ANSI/chunk clause therefore does not apply. Judge C&#39;s reason: an individual fetch carries no explicit AbortSignal. That does not decide the criterion. The readiness wait itself is capped by the loop bound and ends when the child dies. The guidance names no scenario in which a server accepts a connection and never answers, and the candidate produces no such server. Failing on that would mean failing on a hypothetical input. Judge C says each awaited fetch lacks its own timeout. The clause asks that the readiness wait is bounded, and the cited loop bounds it with an attempt cap, a delay, a dead-child exit and a final throw.
